_meta.purpose: Embedded seed pool (#88/#93). Consumed when bank+cache are dry. NEVER calls AI.

questions.question_text: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.explanation: The Berlin Wall fell on November 9, 1989.
questions.saviez_vous: The wall had separated East from West Berlin since 1961.

questions.question_text: In which year did Christopher Columbus reach the Americas?
questions.explanation: Columbus landed in the Bahamas on October 12, 1492.
questions.saviez_vous: He thought he had reached the East Indies in Asia.

questions.question_text: Which event triggered the start of World War I in 1914?
questions.explanation: The Sarajevo assassination on June 28, 1914 set off the alliance system.
questions.saviez_vous: The Archduke was shot by Gavrilo Princip, a young Serbian nationalist.

questions.question_text: Which empire was the largest contiguous land empire in history?
questions.explanation: The 13th-century Mongol Empire covered ~24 million km² in one connected stretch.
questions.saviez_vous: The British Empire was bigger overall but spread across non-adjacent territories.

questions.question_text: How many players are on a football (soccer) team on the pitch?
questions.explanation: A team fields 11 players: 1 goalkeeper and 10 outfield players.
questions.saviez_vous: FIFA caps how many substitutes a team can name for a match.

questions.question_text: Which city hosted the 2024 Summer Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Paris hosted the Summer Olympics from July 26 to August 11, 2024.
questions.saviez_vous: It was the third time Paris hosted the Summer Olympics.

questions.question_text: Which of these team sports averages the highest combined score per game?
questions.explanation: NBA basketball games regularly exceed 200 combined points.
questions.saviez_vous: Soccer averages roughly 2.5 goals per game.

questions.question_text: What is the official marathon distance?
questions.explanation: Since 1921 the official distance has been fixed at 42.195 km.
questions.saviez_vous: The exact distance dates back to the 1908 London Olympics.

questions.question_text: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was chosen in 1908 as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
questions.saviez_vous: It is one of the few capitals purpose-built from scratch.

questions.question_text: Which is the world's largest ocean?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean spans about 165 million km².
questions.saviez_vous: It alone covers more than half of all ocean surface on Earth.

questions.question_text: Which country spans the most time zones (territories included)?
questions.explanation: France covers 12 time zones thanks to its overseas territories.
questions.saviez_vous: Russia has 11 zones on its mainland alone.

questions.question_text: Which country has been the world's most populous since 2023?
questions.explanation: India overtook China in 2023 according to UN estimates.
questions.saviez_vous: China's population is now declining due to its age structure.

questions.question_text: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa between 1503 and 1519.
questions.saviez_vous: The painting hangs in the Louvre Museum in Paris.

questions.question_text: Which artist painted The Starry Night?
questions.explanation: Van Gogh painted The Starry Night in 1889 at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence.
questions.saviez_vous: The painting is held at the MoMA in New York.

questions.question_text: Which art movement did Pablo Picasso co-found with Georges Braque?
questions.explanation: Picasso and Braque founded Cubism around 1907-1908.
questions.saviez_vous: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon (1907) is considered the breakthrough cubist work.

questions.question_text: Who sculpted the Statue of Liberty?
questions.explanation: Bartholdi sculpted it; Eiffel only designed the internal iron framework.
questions.saviez_vous: France gifted the statue to the United States in 1886.

questions.question_text: Modern pizza originated in which country?
questions.explanation: Modern pizza was born in Naples in the 18th century.
questions.saviez_vous: The Margherita is said to have been created in 1889 to honour Queen Margherita.

questions.question_text: Sushi originated in which country?
questions.explanation: Sushi is a traditional Japanese dish.
questions.saviez_vous: Modern nigiri sushi was born in 19th-century Edo (now Tokyo).

questions.question_text: Which of these spices is the most expensive by weight?
questions.explanation: Saffron requires ~150,000 flowers to yield 1 kg, making it extremely costly.
questions.saviez_vous: Each crocus only produces three stigmas, harvested by hand.

questions.question_text: Where did the croissant originate?
questions.explanation: The croissant descends from the Viennese Kipferl; it was popularised later in France.
questions.saviez_vous: Austrian August Zang opened a Viennese bakery in Paris in 1839.

questions.question_text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: "Au" comes from the Latin "aurum", meaning gold.
questions.saviez_vous: Gold is one of the rarest elements in Earth's crust.

questions.question_text: Which planet is nicknamed the "red planet"?
questions.explanation: Mars owes its colour to iron oxide on its surface.
questions.saviez_vous: Mars hosts the largest known volcano in the solar system: Olympus Mons.

questions.question_text: Which chemical element is the most abundant in the universe?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen makes up about 75% of the baryonic mass of the universe.
questions.saviez_vous: It is the fuel of stars, which fuse it into helium.

questions.question_text: What colour is an octopus's blood?
questions.explanation: It is blue because its oxygen carrier is haemocyanin, which contains copper.
questions.saviez_vous: Vertebrate blood is red because of iron-based haemoglobin.

questions.question_text: Who directed the 1997 film "Titanic"?
questions.explanation: James Cameron directed Titanic, released in 1997.
questions.saviez_vous: The film won 11 Oscars, tied with Ben-Hur and The Return of the King.

questions.question_text: Which actor plays the title role in "Forrest Gump" (1994)?
questions.explanation: Tom Hanks plays Forrest Gump and won the Best Actor Oscar for it.
questions.saviez_vous: Tom Hanks won back-to-back Best Actor Oscars (Philadelphia 1994, Forrest Gump 1995).

questions.question_text: What Oscar record do Ben-Hur, Titanic, and The Return of the King share?
questions.explanation: Each won 11 Oscars — the all-time record.
questions.saviez_vous: The Return of the King won 11 out of 11 nominations.

questions.question_text: Which film is considered the first feature-length "talkie"?
questions.explanation: The Jazz Singer (1927) launched mainstream sound cinema.
questions.saviez_vous: The term "talkies" came into use after this film to label sound movies.

questions.question_text: What is the largest living land animal?
questions.explanation: The African bush elephant can weigh up to 6 tonnes.
questions.saviez_vous: An elephant's trunk contains around 40,000 muscles.

questions.question_text: Which is the fastest land animal?
questions.explanation: The cheetah can reach top speeds of about 110 km/h.
questions.saviez_vous: It can only sustain that speed for a few hundred metres.

questions.question_text: Which mammal is famous for laying eggs?
questions.explanation: The platypus is a monotreme mammal — it lays eggs.
questions.saviez_vous: Echidnas are the only other egg-laying mammals.

questions.question_text: Is the shark a fish or a mammal?
questions.explanation: Sharks are cartilaginous fish — they have gills, not lungs.
questions.saviez_vous: Don't confuse them with whales and dolphins, which are mammals.
